analysis: Documentation-only PR: docs/reference/configuration.md adds head lines 320-322 documenting three DARKBLOOM_NEMOTRON_SUPER_MTP* env vars, plus an adjacent DARKBLOOM_NEMOTRON_SUPER_MAX_CONCURRENT row at line 323 (the patch excerpt was truncated, so I could not confirm that row is new). docs/reference/nemotron-super-image-formats.md is a new file; I saw only the truncated patch excerpt of it and no numbered head text. No code, endpoint or control changes are in the supplied evidence. The new rows state that these are opt-in, off by default, parsed from exact values, not forwarded to LaunchAgents, and that the speculating owner refuses media. That is consistent with TB-007 and T-056: they claim no secrecy or correctness guarantee. They also leave the attestation, authorization and App Attest boundaries (TB-011, T-052/T-054) untouched. The prefix-cache (T-041) interactions are not altered by these rows. The documented env flags are process-local operator inputs read inside the attested process; whether they affect the attested build is outside the supplied evidence. Nothing in the supplied text shows a new trust boundary, data exposure or weakened mitigation. The inline image decoder (PNG/JPEG parsing in provider-swift/.../NemotronSuperImageDecode.swift) is the parsing attack surface for an adversarial consumer, but only its documentation is visible here, so the code itself needs separate review if it ships in the same change set. needs_deeper_review is true because the image-format doc was only partially visible and the underlying source files were not supplied.
